# Cost Guard

Starts a local Web server and opens your browser for OpenCode sessions, prompts,
pricing, Token Mix and quotas.

## Requirements

Requires Python 3.11+ and OpenCode on Windows and macOS.
Use the tray/menu **Exit Cost Guard** action to stop the application.
Keep `cache/` when updating or moving a stopped installation.

While connected, Web prioritizes the visible page and warms others slowly, including all four
Accounts CCost chart periods. Watch and Mini update independently; session details load on demand.

## Windows

Start [windows/Cost-Guard-Web.cmd](windows/Cost-Guard-Web.cmd).

## macOS

Start [macos/Cost-Guard-Web.command](macos/Cost-Guard-Web.command).

## Legacy

Terminal reports and Watch: `windows/Legacy` and `macos/Legacy`.

# Cost Guard development

Product code, executable tests, fixtures, developer tooling and machine-read
policies stay in this source repository. Building, testing and running Cost Guard
do not require access to the private backlog.

Project architecture, backlog, journal and the development guide are maintained
in [the private development repository](https://github.com/qstoffe/cost-guard-backlog):

- [Development guide](https://github.com/qstoffe/cost-guard-backlog/blob/main/development/README.md)
- [Architecture and module contracts](https://github.com/qstoffe/cost-guard-backlog/blob/main/development/architecture/OVERVIEW.md)
- [Code/test map](https://github.com/qstoffe/cost-guard-backlog/blob/main/development/architecture/modules/CODE_MAP.md)
- [Journal](https://github.com/qstoffe/cost-guard-backlog/blob/main/development/journal/INDEX.md)

Source-local areas:

- `tests/`: executable checks, deterministic fixtures and maintained integration probes.
- `tests/policies/`: machine-read validation policies; do not silently raise limits.
- `tools/`: development checks and diagnostics implementation.
- `user-tools/`: human-facing diagnostics launchers.
- `logs/`: ignored, on-demand runtime errors, crashes, recovery events and
  `diagnostics/cost-guard-diagnostics.zip`; never included in package copies.

Web warm history is in the installation's ignored
`cache/cost-guard-cache-v2.sqlite3`. An in-place Git update keeps the directory.
Exit Cost Guard before moving the whole installation so no process is writing
its SQLite files. A new source-only folder starts cold; it does not search
other installations or automatically copy private evidence.

Quiet maintenance starts 60 seconds after Web readiness or Legacy presentation,
then attempts retention once per day, independently of cache/source readiness.
Only recognized, unchanged regular files strictly older than 30 days are removed
from this tree and legacy root `logs/` / `diagnostics/`. Active recovery state,
unrecognized files, links and uncertain/in-flight ZIP staging survive. Bundling
does not prune recent logs or historic ZIPs. ZIP `logs/` members remain readable,
with distinct legacy prefixes and duplicate contents omitted. Custom Diagnostics
output stays caller-owned. Managed Web lock/auth/lifecycle/diagnostics and its
private error logs remain in per-user application data, outside this contract.

`repository.json` retains source release settings and the private backlog locator.
`applied-contract.json` identifies the adopted installed development contract.
Contract Sync changes no product behavior, release policy or backlog counters.

Executable boundaries live in `src/entrypoints/`: `desktop.py` routes ordinary
desktop startup, `web.py` owns managed/developer Web dispatch, and `cli.py` is the
explicit Legacy terminal entry. Each supports direct execution from any working
directory; `python -m src.entrypoints.<mode>` works from the installation root.
Keep user-facing Windows/macOS launchers at their existing paths. Launcher tests
use disposable installs and redirected/hosted-only harnesses, not workstation UI.

`src/version.py` owns the functional version and release date. Validate runtime
version output with `python development/tools/validate_package.py --working-tree`
and run all registered regressions with
`python development/tools/run_tests.py --suite full`. README is a tiny Web quick
start, not a version binding. Git retains release history; no prose history or
root documentation tree is shipped. The validator rejects retired root wrappers
and documentation while retaining package/privacy, import and size gates.

Human date/time text uses `ReportView.formatDateTime` in
[`src/web/assets/render.js`](../src/web/assets/render.js) and `format_date_time`
in [`src/analysis/timezones.py`](../src/analysis/timezones.py). Use a named
`DateTimeMode` and the effective configured IANA zone for epoch milliseconds;
pass source calendar days directly in `DATE` mode. The ordinary package
validator and Web display tests check formatter ownership. See the
[date/time presentation rule](https://github.com/qstoffe/cost-guard-backlog/blob/main/development/architecture/USER_FACING_UX_POLICY.md#date-and-time-presentation).

# Synthetic fixtures

This directory owns deterministic, non-secret test fixtures for Cost Guard development.

Real OpenCode databases, auth files, credentials, personal session exports, runtime caches and other user data MUST NOT be committed here. Later steps may add small synthetic V1 SQLite databases and V2 HTTP/event payload fixtures whose provenance and purpose are documented by their tests.

# Executable validation policies

`file-budgets.json` is consumed by the source-local package validator and tests.
Its limits were moved unchanged from the former governance directory.

Do not silently raise limits, rebaseline exceptions or weaken validation to make
a change pass. Refactor the responsible code or obtain an explicit scoped decision.
Documentary architecture/policies and historical results live in the private
development repository; source tests and builds must not depend on that access.

# Configuration fixtures

Small non-secret fixtures that characterize v77-compatible recursive JSONC merging,
explicit-null behavior, legacy pricing-cache normalization, and fail-closed unknown settings.

# Reviewed model research fixture

`reviewed-models.json` retains the public source URLs and the exact
publisher/model/evidence/confidence fields exercised by the effort-help regression.
It is extracted from the 2026-11-13 research snapshot present in source commit
`38c2269d8ef3cb06c6476cf1a685c790d42ebd3f`, not fetched from the private backlog.
The complete historical attachment remains unchanged in the private archive.

This is test metadata, not deployed runtime defaults or evidence of an executed
request's reasoning effort. Counts and unresolved cases remain independently
asserted in the test. No test performs a network request to these source URLs.

# Synthetic OpenAI TLS regression chain

These are disposable localhost test certificates and a **synthetic server key**,
not credentials or certificates from a workstation/provider. Generated offline
with .NET `CertificateRequest`; no machine certificate store was changed.

- `root.pem`: synthetic server-authentication trust root, valid 2020–2045.
- `unrelated-root.pem`: an independent synthetic root for untrusted-chain rejection.
- `server.pem`: localhost leaf and current intermediate, valid 2020–2045.
- `expired-intermediate.pem`: the same intermediate subject/key, expired in 2021.
- `expired-server.pem`: expired localhost leaf and the current intermediate.
- `synthetic-server-key.pem`: only the disposable localhost leaf's private key.

The server supplies its current chain. Loading the expired intermediate beside
the root reproduces OpenSSL's trusted-first expiry failure. The Windows ROOT-only
context must succeed without admitting expired leaves, untrusted chains or a
hostname mismatch. Everything stays on loopback; no package or external tool is
needed to execute the tests.

# OpenCode V1 fixture contract

`schema.sql` is a deliberately minimal synthetic legacy projection schema for the
V1 adapter. Tests create temporary SQLite databases at runtime and insert small
JSON message/part payloads matching the semantics consumed by Cost Guard.

No real user OpenCode database is copied into the repository. The fixture keeps
adapter tests deterministic and proves that production reads are independent of
an installed `opencode` executable.

# Persisted V2 cancellation error

## Summary

Read-only inspection of the reported second prompt confirmed the current V2
assistant error shape above: `type: aborted`, no `name`, `finish: error`, a
completed timestamp, and no tokens on the terminal assistant message. The old
normalizer returned `dict`, losing the cancellation discriminator. The message
is deliberately redacted; recognition must depend on the explicit type, not its
text. Session identities, prompts and assistant content are not retained.

Synthetic CLI text at 120 columns; no live source or browser evidence.
Numeric prompt/Watch grids retain their minimum widths (no clipping);
Token Mix cells wrap, and narrow historical tables use labeled rows.

* Tokens: known Input / Cached input / Cache write / Output volume, including reasoning in Output; K/M/B are rounded
  display only. ? marks incomplete telemetry; N/A means no known categories.
* Input / Cached input / Cache write / Output: Token Mix % of the model/publisher's token volume (Output includes
  reasoning) and its CCost.
* CCost: reference token valuation priced per request, not actual billing; ? marks partial pricing.
* Prompts: unique user prompts where the model contributed usage; one prompt can count on several rows.
* Calls: model requests attributed to the model, including tool-loop, subagent and compaction requests.

* History includes OpenCode usage data that is still available; deleted or pruned history is not reconstructed.
* Historical publisher shares use pooled shown requests, not the 100-slot comparison prior. Prompts are distinct within
  each model/publisher; mixed prompts can appear in several rows, so row prompt counts are not additive. Unknown /
  unverified is not an account provider.
